audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating liquidity as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $208.057 million bridge balance ($8.41 per share); required operating portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity bridge adds cash and marketable securities dollar-for-dollar after valuing operating owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 1, 2025, the Company divested a portion of its marketable securities portfolio to increase cash and cash equivalents liquidity to satisfy working capital obligations, selling $7.2 million in equity securities and $24.4 million in corporate and municipal bonds.
audit_findings.explanation: No specific bridge error is demonstrated, but the filing shows that securities were liquidated to satisfy working-capital obligations. Because the entire $208.057 million bridge equals about 23% of BASE equity value, a substantial operating-cash requirement could materially reduce the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Calculate normalized minimum cash using monthly working-capital, payment-settlement, capital-spending, insurance and liquidity data; rerun all scenarios with only demonstrably surplus cash and securities.

audit_findings.title: Zero debt does not establish that the latest-quarter bridge captured every senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Known letter-of-credit face amount $6.7 million ($0.27 per share); any incremental senior claim unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An economic claim not already reflected in owner earnings or the equity bridge would reduce value attributable to common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The letters of credit are maintained primarily to support performance, payment, deposit or surety obligations of the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: No omitted liability is demonstrated. Letters of credit are contingent support instruments rather than an automatic $6.7 million debt deduction, and the identified amount is only about 0.7% of BASE equity value. However, the record does not reconcile all commitments against amounts already captured in owner earnings, so the materiality of any additional claim remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 liability ledger, commitments, litigation, taxes, self-insurance, SERP and acquisition obligations; rerun only for claims not recorded in liabilities or already expensed through owner earnings.

audit_findings.title: SERP investments must not be counted as unencumbered cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 bridge misclassification; $35.584 million SERP investment is separately reported against a $35.583 million postretirement obligation
audit_findings.mechanism: Including the SERP asset without its matching obligation would improperly increase the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company chooses to invest in the underlying mutual fund investments to offset the liability associated with the non-qualified deferred compensation plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The demonstrated bridge of $208.057 million exactly equals June 2026 cash of $103.529 million plus marketable securities of $104.528 million. It therefore excludes the separately reported SERP investment. The $0.001 million asset-liability difference is immaterial relative to $911 million of BASE equity value.
audit_findings.action: No valuation rerun is needed; preserve the current mapping and continue excluding the SERP investment unless its matching obligation is also included.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require reinvestment omitted from forward owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 capital spending $205.2 million versus $124.789 million depreciation, a computed $80.411 million excess; first-half 2026 purchases $87.951 million versus $63.509 million depreciation, a computed $24.442 million excess
audit_findings.mechanism: Required maintenance, modernization or growth investment reduces forward owner earnings supporting the projected growth rates.
audit_findings.evidence: Property and equipment purchases totaled $205.2 million in 2025, $168.5 million in 2024 and $104.0 million in 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate that reinvestment was omitted, because it does not provide the maintenance-versus-growth capital bridge used to derive the $50.0 million anchor. Materiality is nevertheless established: 2025 spending above depreciation was about 1.6 times anchor owner earnings, and the supplied 4.8% return on net tangible assets raises doubt that 3%-5% growth can be obtained without substantial additional investment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the owner-earnings calculation to total capital spending by maintenance, modernization, replacement and expansion categories; estimate reinvestment required for each growth case and rerun all scenarios after deducting it.

audit_findings.title: The reported history and anchor remain exposed to an unresolved control weakness
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed corrections include $5.502 million after-tax opening retained earnings at 2022, $2.974 million of 2023 net income, $3.918 million of 2024 net income and $3.508 million for the first 39 weeks of 2025; residual owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncorrected inventory and cost-of-sales errors could overstate historical or anchor owner earnings and influence normalization or growth judgments.
audit_findings.evidence: Management concluded that there was a material weakness in internal controls due to the incorrect recording of certain overstated inventory amounts and that our internal controls over financial reporting were not designed to prevent or detect a material error as of December 27, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: A historical accounting error is demonstrated, but the supplied 2023-2025 statements were corrected, the 2025 financial statements received an unqualified audit opinion, and management reported the weakness remediated by June 2026. The remaining concern is an unresolved possibility concerning earlier years or further undetected errors. Its valuation effect cannot be established without the year-by-year owner-earnings reconciliation; the restatement itself did not change reported operating cash flow for the periods shown.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every owner-earnings year to the corrected filings, verify the $50.0 million anchor against audited 2025 figures, and review post-remediation physical-count and control-testing evidence; rerun if any corrected OE amount differs.

audit_findings.title: A property-disposition gain may remain in normalized owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $7.840 million pre-tax or a computed $5.927 million after tax; approximately $83.3 million or $3.37 per share of BASE value if fully embedded in the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring disposal gain left in the $50.0 million anchor would be capitalized through projected owner earnings and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: These increases were partially offset by a net gain on the disposition of fixed assets related to real estate property sales, which reduced operating, general, and administrative expenses in 2025 compared with 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The $7.840 million 2025 fixed-asset disposition gain is demonstrated, but its inclusion in the supplied owner-earnings anchor is not. Using the filed 24.4% tax rate, its after-tax amount equals about 11.9% of the anchor; applying the BASE operating-value-to-anchor multiple produces a potential value effect of about 9.1% of BASE equity value, which is material.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $50.0 million anchor calculation and remove all disposition gains and associated tax effects if present; then rerun every scenario without changing the supplied growth, discount-rate or share inputs.
